stem: 2. Find A∪B, A∩B, A–B and B–A for the following sets.

entries.question: A = {2, 6, 10, 14} and B={2, 5, 14, 16}
steps: List distinct elements: A = {2, 6, 10, 14} and B = {2, 5, 14, 16}.
The union contains all distinct elements from either set, so A∪B = {2, 6, 10, 14, 5, 16}; the intersection contains elements common to both, so A∩B = {2, 14}.
Remove elements of B from A to obtain A−B = {6, 10}; remove elements of A from B to obtain B−A = {5, 16}.

The union contains all distinct elements from either set, so A∪B = {a, b, c, e, u, i, o}; the intersection contains elements common to both, so A∩B = {a, e, u}.
Remove elements of B from A to obtain A−B = {b, c}; remove elements of A from B to obtain B−A = {i, o}.
entries.answer: A∪B = {a, b, c, e, u, i, o}; A∩B = {a, e, u}; A−B = {b, c}; B−A = {i, o}.
